UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile and academic information within the CyberDoc application. This data is distinct from authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. Corresponds to the user's authentication UID.

firstName.description: The first name of the user, used for personalization and document cover pages.

lastName.description: The last name of the user, used for personalization and document cover pages.

email.description: The email address of the user.

university.description: The name of the university the user attends, displayed on document cover pages.

faculty.description: The faculty the user belongs to, displayed on document cover pages.

promotion.description: The academic promotion (e.g., year, level) of the user, displayed on document cover pages.

credits.description: The current credit balance of the user, used for service payments.

role.description: The role of the user within the application, defining their permissions.

DocumentSettings.title: DocumentSettings
DocumentSettings.description: Defines the formatting and styling settings applied to a specific document.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DocumentSettings entity.

font.description: The font style chosen for the document content.

fontSize.description: The font size in points for the document content.

lineHeight.description: The line spacing (e.g., '1', '1.5', '2') for the document content.

margins.description: The margin setting for the document (e.g., 'normal', 'reduced').

Document.title: Document
Document.description: Represents an academic document created by a user, including its content, formatting, service choices, and payment status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Document entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who owns this document. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Document)

documentSettingsId.description: Reference to the DocumentSettings applied to this document. (Relationship: DocumentSettings 1:N Document)

title.description: The optional title of the document.

course.description: The academic course associated with the document.

professor.description: The professor or instructor for whom the document is intended.

content.description: The raw content of the document, supporting Markdown and LaTeX syntax.

serviceType.description: The type of service selected for the document (e.g., 'simple' for PDF, 'nb' for black & white print, 'color' for color print).

hasCoverPage.description: Indicates whether a professional cover page is included with the document.

hasBinding.description: Indicates whether binding is applied to the physical document (if printed).

pageCount.description: The estimated number of pages in the formatted document.

price.description: The total calculated price for the document services in local currency.

isPaid.description: Indicates whether the document services have been paid for.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the document was initially created.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. The document ID `{userId}` must match the Firebase Authentication UID of the user. Includes denormalized 'role' for potential future permissioning logic. Fields such as 'credits' are directly updated.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, corresponding to their Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Stores academic documents created by a specific user. The `{userId}` in the path indicates ownership. Document settings (font, fontSize, lineHeight, margins) are denormalized and embedded directly into the document, within a 'settings' field, to ensure Authorization Independence and simplify atomic operations.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this document, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

params.name: documentId
params.description: The unique identifier for the document itself.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes secure, scalable, and debuggable authorization rules by adhering strictly to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation.

**User Profiles:** User profiles are stored in a top-level collection `/users/{userId}`. This path-based ownership means a user's profile document ID (`{userId}`) directly corresponds to their authentication UID (`request.auth.uid`), making security rules extremely simple and explicit. Access to a user's own profile is granted by matching `request.auth.uid == userId`.

**Documents:** Academic documents are stored in a subcollection under the user's profile: `/users/{userId}/documents/{documentId}`. This hierarchical structure establishes clear, path-based ownership for each document, where `{userId}` in the path is the owner's UID. This directly supports the 'Private Data' and 'Hierarchical Paths for User-Owned Data' access models. The `Document` entity's `userId` field also explicitly stores the owner's UID, providing a redundant check that can be leveraged by rules, though the path-based rule is primary.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**

*   **DocumentSettings Denormalization:** Critically, the `DocumentSettings` (font, size, margins, etc.) are **fully denormalized and embedded** within each `Document` document under a `settings` field. This decision is based on the application code's implementation (where `settings: DocSettings` is part of `DocumentData` passed to `addDoc`). This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in Firestore security rules to fetch related `DocumentSettings` from a separate collection when creating, reading, or updating a `Document`. As a result, operations on `Document` documents are atomic and do not suffer from the complexities or potential security vulnerabilities introduced by multi-document reads in rules. This directly addresses the 'Authorization Independence (CRITICAL)' mandate.
*   **No Cross-Collection Dependencies:** Neither `UserProfile` nor `Document` documents rely on `get()` calls to other collections for their authorization logic. All necessary authorization context (`request.auth.uid`, path wildcards, and denormalized fields) is available directly within the `request` or `resource` objects.

**Query-Access Patterns (QAPs) and Structural Segregation:**

*   **`/users/{userId}`:** For user profiles, the QAP is simple: `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid)`. The security rules will allow `read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. This ensures that a user can only query and modify their *own* profile. Listing all user profiles would be blocked unless an 'admin' role (implemented via DBAC as a separate collection or explicit rule) is present.
*   **`/users/{userId}/documents/{documentId}`:** For documents, the QAP for listing documents is `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid).collection('documents').orderBy('createdAt', 'desc')`. The security rules for this path will simply be `allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. This perfectly aligns with the QAP, as the query explicitly includes the `request.auth.uid` in the path, ensuring that a user can *only* list, create, and manage their own documents. There is no ambiguity, and the rules are not functioning as filters, but rather as clear authorization gates. This structure intrinsically supports secure `list` operations without exposing data that the user is not authorized to see, even if a malicious query attempts to bypass the client-side `where` clause.

This design leverages structural ownership and denormalization to create a highly secure, performant, and easily auditable Firestore database, fully compliant with the specified principles.
